notes: The GTR is reachable through E-utilities with no login, but the data is too thin and too coarse for the thesis. The esearch counts are free-text hits, not instrument-field counts. 'NovaSeq 6000' returned 130 records, 'NovaSeq X' returned 12, and the broad 'NovaSeq' term returned 404. A few thousand clinical tests in GTR is a small, self-reported sample. Labs rarely update the instrument field. Test 560898 is a Caris whole-transcriptome RNA-seq test that lists the NovaSeq 6000, and its record was last updated 2022-12-27, so it is stale. The esummary output has no update-date field and no instrument field, only the test name and the lab. Getting the instrument and date means fetching each record page or the bulk FTP files, which I did not do. I could not run the bulk-FTP version-history check (it would need a bash or python tool I did not have). The 12 'NovaSeq X' hits include Univ. Michigan single-gene tests, Mass General Brigham, Integrated Genetics (Labcorp, MaterniT NIPT) and an Indian lab. That fits NIPT and small hospital labs moving first. But a 130 vs 12 count split mostly reflects when labs registered their tests, not the live installed base. I did not rank the 10 largest 6000-only labs. The esearch output gives IDs only, and I only summarized the 10 X records plus one 6000 record.
how_to_mine: Low priority. If you pursue it, download ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pub/GTR/data/test_version.gz and test_condition_gene.txt. Filter the methodology and instrument text for 'NovaSeq 6000' vs 'NovaSeq X', then group by lab and keep only the records with last-update dates in 2025-26. Check whether any lab's record history shows a switch from 6000 to X. Expect to find few switches. Use this only as a weak, directional check on who the remaining 6000 users are.

items.label: 1A
items.claim: Self-reported GTR test records still list the NovaSeq 6000 about 11x more often than the NovaSeq X, though this is a stale-registration artifact and a weak signal.
items.detail: An NCBI E-utilities free-text search on db=gtr (12 Oct 2026) returned 130 hits for 'NovaSeq 6000' and 12 for 'NovaSeq X'. Test 560898 (Caris whole-transcriptome RNA-seq) still lists the 6000 and was last updated 2022-12-27. Labs seldom revise this field, so the ratio overstates the live 6000 share.
items.why_new: No GTR instrument-field count or lab-level 6000 vs X split is in the known evidence.
